utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Mr. Registrar, may you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances for today, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Matthias Neuner, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. [Microphone not activated] For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to the learned friends from the Prosecution. Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Delic, and Lejla Gluhic as legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You made a declaration yesterday to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. You made --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are aware that you are still bound by that declaration, but it's my duty to remind you that indeed you are. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic, you had just started your cross-examination yesterday. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Hasanagic. I hope that you are well-rested and that today we can proceed in an easy manner.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we discussed the fact that you were a trained professional soldier but that you do not have any associates and colleagues who were trained in professional. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you a document. It is of a temporary war formation or unit. But before that, for the benefit of the Bench, could you confirm that a temporary wartime formation is a document which regulates the structure of a certain unit; that it is of a temporary character because it is valid until a new establishment or a new formation is issued? Is -- am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like the witness to see document D417. For the record, this is a temporary wartime formation of the command of division together with the staff units. The number is BH100.301.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you take a look at the first page, please. Do you agree this is the document issued in December 1994, as is stated on the first page?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see this document in its -- in this form, but I do think this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at page 2 of this document. Thank you. Do you agree that this page shows that the commander of the General Staff of the army adopted on the 23rd of September, 1994 this temporary wartime establishment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like you to take a look at the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if this could be centred or lined in such a way that we can see it. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, please take a look at this organisational chart to make sure -- whether you agree that the division was organised in a manner depicted here during the relevant period in 1994/1995.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can the witness see anything? Are you able to read what's inside there, sir? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is much better. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the schematic of our division, the organisational chart.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to -- you to take a look at page 4 in the B/C/S version, which is page 4 in the English version as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I -- can I interrupt, Madam Vidovic? Page 3 at line 15, it's written "23rd of September, 1994." It should be "December 1994."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may see the page again. Could we have that page appear on the screen, please, in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's in the -- it's in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. It's supposed to be December 1994. This is how I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, no, you said so, but the transcript -- I just want to correct the transcript. Thank you very much. You may proceed, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Maybe the usher can turn the next page of this document. Page 4. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at this page of the temporary wartime establishment. Here we have an outlook, the division command with staff units. And there are certain columns. In the first, it states: "Appointment." Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in the next column we have the abbreviation "OF"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this an acronym for "officers"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The next column is -- are "non-commissioned officers."

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at these figures here. Do you agree that in the "OF" column, denoting "officers," there are certain figures showing how many officers the division command ought to have and the headquarters command, then communications, et cetera, et cetera? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have the next page of this document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this column of "officers," do you agree that we have 76 as a total, which means as per temporary establishment, it was envisaged for the division command to have 76 officers? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those officers were supposed to be military academy graduates to be officers, as per rules and regulations.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An officer is supposed to be a military academy graduate.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But what was the reality in the 35th Division's command was that out of the 76 envisaged, only 3 had a degree from the military academy.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe three. Maybe four or five, but roughly this would be the figure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will show you the names. We will sort this out. Nesad Sabic had a degree. He was chief of staff. Semir Hamzic, assistant for logistics. And you. And we are discussing the command of your division. Do anybody -- do you know of anybody else except for the three of you who was a military academy graduate in the division command?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't remember anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So out of the 76 officers envisaged in the command, only a handful were professionally trained soldiers; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, please understand me. I'm talking about the real state of affairs in the division. Is it true that in the division you really had only three/four officers with a diploma from the military academy?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The 35th Division in the period 1995 had 12 thousand soldiers; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, between 11.000 and a half and 12.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Per establishment, you were supposed to have three mountain brigades; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Each of those brigades was supposed to have 120 trained officers; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember this piece of information, but those were supposed to be trained, schooled officers. I can't remember the figure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Do you agree with the following piece of information: You know the structure of those brigades well. You know the people who commanded them. You know the command staff of the brigades under your command.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right if I would say that only the commander of the 329th Brigade, Fehim Skulj was a military academy graduate?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Haris Catic [Realtime transcript read in error "Feris Hadzic"] also had a degree. I can't remember about Skulj.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, but you agree with me, don't you, that people with military training in those brigades were a rarity?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the 35th Division, you had three manoeuvre battalions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In each of them, there were supposed to be 15 trained officers. Can you accept that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Out of those officers in the battalions, only the -- that person that you mentioned a while ago, Mr. Catic, was a military academy graduate. Can you accept that as a fact?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, in accordance with this establishment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. I just saw that the name of the officer which Mr. Hasanagic mentioned a while ago, I believe it was Haris Catic is not captured well in the transcript. On page 7, line 15 it says "Feris Hadzic." If this could please be corrected by my learned colleague with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, answering my question, you also added that another officer had military training, Haris Catic.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And later on I mentioned that he was in one of the manoeuvre battalions.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So his name is Catic Haris or Haris Catic. So the command of the 35th Division, together with its subordinated units, was supposed to have some 500 trained officers. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact figures, but those officers should have been trained.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You agree that this is a large number of trained officers.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in reality, there was only a handful. Five, to be exact, if -- the way we list them. Could you accept that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So only a few of your associates were trained to understand what the system of control and command meant; am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were supposed to know the system of control and command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I know that they were supposed to, but I am inquiring about the facts on the ground. Were they trained to know what that meant? Were they trained -- did they know that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took over personnel when I came from the operational group, and this division grew out of that operational group and the personnel that I had was such that, depending on the mission and task, they were trained and they were not trained at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that a person who is not professionally trained, that such a person cannot report in the proper manner? An officer who has not graduated from the military academy or does not have military training, they cannot report properly or prepare a proper report.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, such a person does not know how to prepare a proper report.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have -- may we tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 482.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a brief question relating to the situation in the division. Concerning security organs in the division and in the units belonging to it. Mr. Hasanagic, would you agree that neither a division nor the brigades had experienced officers in the field of military security affairs? In other words, it did not have officers with military knowledge or experience in this particular domain.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the battalion, brigade, and divisions, the security organs had no training for these particular tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to dwell now on two specific persons whose reports are essential for certain issues that I will go back to, and you were also asked about this yesterday by the Prosecutor. Please, let us look at the security organ of the 328th Brigade. At the head of this organ was Mr. Enes Malicbegovic. In fact, he was an assistant for security affairs. Enes Malicbegovic. He was not a military person at all in terms of his educational background. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that this was in the 328th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I'm going to ask you about Mr. Imamovic, who was in your division. Am I right to say that he, before he became a security officer in your unit or in the Operations Group Bosnia had had no military training for this particular task nor any experience in that area?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Similarly, he didn't finish any courses or attend any seminars for this kind of job. And I am talking about security.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he came --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the post of the person in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, the interpreters --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, can you repeat the post from which Mr. Imamovic came and assumed duties in the 35th Division. Can you please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that, he was the commander of the 311 Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The purpose of my question was that at the time while he was discharging these duties in the area of security in Bosna OG and in the 35th Division, he had not attended any training courses or seminars, because there was no time for that. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Hamdija Sljuka?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late September 1995, he came and replaced the security officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So he replaced Mr. Fadil Imamovic in that job; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Neither he had any professional training, military training in security issues. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was a lawyer. As for the rest of it, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Vidovic, could you please wait for the translation to be over. And, Witness, please wait for the translation to be over before you answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right to assert that in September 1995, certain personnel were replaced in the military security services of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Imamovic left and his position was taken over by Mr. Sljuka.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that these replacements took place simultaneously in the 3rd Corps as well? If you know about that.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What I would like to ask you now is the following: Is it true that operations officers or officers of military security should be, as we say, the eyes and the ears of the commander? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "eyes and ears," but anyway, they should have had all the relevant information about the situation in the territory that they would then pass on to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is particularly what I meant. You were not the person to go in the field, to collect intelligence; rather, this intelligence should have been provided to you by the intelligence officer or security officer. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, they were supposed to monitor the situation and inform you properly about the developments and also submit reports to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were also supposed to write reports to their higher superior command. For instance, when this concerned military security affairs.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the professional sense, they were independent and they had their lines of communicating reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, they were supposed to inform you along command lines and professionally along the chain of communication to their superior corps.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please can you repeat your answer. Do you remember my question? Can you please just speak more slowly. The transcript is unable to record this.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. They wrote their reports to their superior in the corps along the professional lines, and they also briefed me as much as was necessary for the purpose of command and control. They estimated which information should be passed on to me and which information should be passed elsewhere, based on their professional knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this additional explanation. Now I would like to ask you the following: Their reports about significant developments should be in writing. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, written reports were being submitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But what I'm asking you is about the rule. If a significant event was in question about which your associates or security assistants or an intelligence officer had information, they should have put this down in writing. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Their report should be properly registered and filed in the archives; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, let me ask you something else. In this courtroom, we had an opportunity to see the Farz plan and map. And if you can only clarify something for us. Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 380. Mr. Hasanagic, I would like just to explain to you that we had an opportunity here to see a large map which was actually a photocopy of the colour original. I'm showing this to you only for the purpose of establishing a certain principle.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can this please be enlarged?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please have this Bosnian version enlarged here, because that's the one that is important. Thank you. Please, would you agree that in the map or -- showing the attack formation here --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Operation plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see the name of a person in the upper left-hand corner. You can clearly see the name of the person who had approved this plan. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please have this map scrolled down so that the witness can look at the bottom part of it. Do you agree that it is clearly shown here the name of the person who signed the map? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, in addition to the person who approved the map, there should be the signature and the stamp, and the same applies to the name of the person who is signing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. However, this is the principle, the general rule applied to the approval of combat operations map -- maps; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please show this whole document to the witness. Can you please just enlarge it a little bit. I would like the witness to look, if possible, and see the area of responsibility of the 35th Division. Can this also be enlarged again, please. A little bit more, please, this particular area here. Very well. So, Witness, can you identify here the area of responsibility of your division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to this map -- can you show to Their Honours - and I think you have an electronic pointer with you - can you indicate the area of responsibility of your division.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please connect these lines, if possible, so that we can see approximately what is exactly encompassed by this zone.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's good. Very well. Mr. Hasanagic, can you tell us approximately the -- how many square kilometres was your area of responsibility at the time that we are talking about, that is, 1995, prior to these combat operations?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but I think it's between 50 and 60 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So that was the area of responsibility -- your area of responsibility. Not square kilometres?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not square kilometres. I am talking about length kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are talking about this line. Would you agree that this was a lot?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have this information in square metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, I'm talking about square kilometres. Would you agree that this was much more, that this was a huge area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In geographical terms, this is an exceptionally forbidden terrain criss-crossed with mountains and difficult to negotiate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is precisely the characteristics, these criss-cross, few roads, lots of woods, scattered villages, and very characteristic features. That applies to the whole Ozren mountain. You have a ridge, then you have a valley, then you have a ridge and valley, et cetera. This is where the 35th Division was, and the elevations varied between 500 and 600 metres up to 1.000 metres. It is also criss-crossed by rivers and streams.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I am suggesting, Mr. Hasanagic, is that the area covered by the 35th Division was extremely difficult in terms of warfare.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You knew that the Muslim villages around Ozren and Vozuca back in 1992, at the beginning of war, had been ethnically cleansed, many of them.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received this information when I took up my duty, and I knew about -- I knew about few purely Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These were -- these people were expelled by the Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the information which I received when I took up my duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In those villages and other points at Ozren, there were artillery positions from which there was constant shelling. There was constant shelling of the territory controlled by the state of -- or, rather, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those features are important. One of them was Blizna, that one could see Zavidovici from and the environs. And there is Djurica Vis and Kvrge. Paljenik was another feature which dominated the area. And they also had artillery pieces there as well as tanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, please slow down, because it is difficult for the transcript to catch up. I'm sorry to say, but we both tend to speak fast.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat if necessary. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There won't be any need for that. Do you agree that from Ozren, Tuzla was shelled and that during the spring of 1995 that shelling caused severe consequences?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially from the positions in the area of Kvrge. After we took up that -- that feature, I was able to see there that there were five or six trucks of spent cartridges that were extracted from the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you constantly suffered losses, soldiers were being killed. I don't mean you personally, but the 35th Division. There were casualties all the time.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It particularly pertained to the 328th Brigade. I cannot recall the exact figure, but over 1.000 of their men were killed in the area. I don't know the exact -- an exact figure, but certainly over 1.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was caused by the activity from Ozren and the Vozuca area. It was the cause of casualties among civilians within your area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Civilians were usually killed from Blizna, Paljenik, and Podsijelovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to tender this map and I ask that it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 483.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you something else. During 1995, in your area of responsibility, the resources, such as fuel, medication, and the rest were used up.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ammunition and other resources, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Such as food, spare parts, and anything that the soldiers or civilians might need; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Such resources depended greatly on the civilian authorities in the surrounding municipalities. First and foremost, that of Zavidovici and Tesanj. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Zavidovici -- Zavidovici, Maglaj, and Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction. Zavidovici, Maglaj, and Kakanj, then. Thank you. I will return to this topic later. I wanted to put certain important questions to you now concerning the El Mujahedin Detachment. Mr. Hasanagic, yesterday the Prosecutor showed you a number -- a large number of documents in which there is mention of the El Mujahedin Detachment. In those documents, the El Mujahedin Detachment is mentioned concerning various aspects that have to do with command and control. Do you remember having seen those documents yesterday?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those documents -- those documents were pieces of paper; however, I have a simple question to put to you. Do you agree that the documents you saw yesterday do not reflect the situation as it was, in terms of command and control over that unit?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many documents do not reflect the situation with the command of that unit for the simple reason --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us go document by document.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to say that I wasn't familiar with the establishment of that unit and many other things that need to be in place in order to be able to command -- control that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hasanagic, we'll go step by step. Yesterday and the day before during your testimony, you did not dispute that the 35th Division by the 3rd Corps decision, that unit was re-subordinated to it for the first time on the 24th October, 1994. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also did not dispute the fact that that unit - and I mean to you, the 35th Division - was again re-subordinated for the purposes of combat activities on the 31st of March, 1995 by the corps command. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was on the 2nd of June, 1995, was it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about that re-subordinate.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry. I just wanted to point out one thing. Maybe the translation was not adequate. It says here on page 21, line 1. The question was: "You also did not dispute the fact that that unit - and I mean to you, the 35th Division - was again re-subordinated" I assume that in the original it should have been the El Mujahedin Detachment. I just wanted to point that out, that the El Mujahedin Detachment was re-subordinated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank the Prosecutor. I asked the witness whether he was disputing that the El Mujahedin Detachment was re-subordinated to the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that so, Witness, and not the other way around?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the cases that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to ask you about the latest case of re-subordination on the 2nd of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, but at this moment, after Mr. Neuner's intervention, the transcript as it reads is simply unclear now. What is the meaning of the question that you put to the witness on page 20, line 22 and what is the correct answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the problem seems to be that we do not have the same page before us. I will have a look. I asked the witness -- if I may have a moment. "You also are not denying that" -- my question was: "You are not denying that the El Mujahedin Detachment was re-subordinated to the 35th Division." That was a question. The witness said "yes." And then I said: "That was on the 2nd of June, 1995." Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Because we started out by establishing that the -- that the El Mujahedin Detachment was re-subordinated to the 35th Division on the 24th of October. Then your next question, which I do not understand, had to do with some subordination for combat which was taking place on the 31st of March, 1995. And then there was another date of 2nd of June, 1995. Now, what happened on these three dates is unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll clear it up with the witness, since it is important. And it seems we're going too fast.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, it is correct - and you testified to that effect yesterday - that by a decision of the 3rd Corps the El Mujahedin Detachment was re-subordinated to you for the first time on the 24th of October, 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- that was the time when the Operations Group Bosna was still in existence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That re-subordination took place by virtue of a 3rd Corps order. The El Mujahedin Detachment was re-subordinated to the Operations Group Bosna on the 24th October 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony yesterday, you confirmed that the 35th Division was formed. Can you tell us when?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 1st of March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st of March, 1995, that is when the 35th Division was formed. By an order of the 3rd Corps command on the 31st of March, 1995, the 3rd Corps command re-subordinated the El Mujahedin Detachment to the 35th Division. [Realtime transcript read in error "The 1st of March, 1995. That is when the 35th Division was formed by an order of the 3rd Corps command on the 31st of March, 1995, the 3rd Corps command re-subordinated the El Mujahedin Detachment to the 35th Division"]

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There was another thing I wanted to ask you. On the 2nd of June, 1995, there was another decision, another order by the 3rd Corps commander that that unit, the El Mujahedin Detachment, be re-subordinated again to the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But why would this -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, you go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But why would this happen twice?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was to be my next question. I wanted to try and clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I'm confused. Page 23, line 7, you say -- that's a question by you, Madam Vidovic: "The 1st of March, 1995. That is when the 35th Division was formed by an order of the 3rd Corps command on the 31st of March, 1995, the 3rd Corps command re-subordinated the El Mujahedin Detachment to the 35th Division." What does the 31st of March relate to? Does it relate to the formation of the 35th Division or does it relate to the re-subordination of the -- of the El Mujahedin to the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is the way it was recorded. I clearly said on the 1st of March, 1995, the 35th Division was formed, and the witness confirmed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 31st of March, 1995, the 3rd Corps re-subordinates the El Mujahedin Detachment to the newly formed division. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we heard other testimony in this case, and I wanted to ask you something in relation to that. If one were to say that you yourself asked that the El Mujahedin Detachment, due to the grave circumstances within your area of responsibility, remain in the area, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will simplify. Did you personally ask the 3rd Corps command in early June 1995 that the El Mujahedin Detachment remain within your AOR and to remain re-subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask for another clarification. In this courtroom, we are not soldiers and certainly not military experts, particularly myself; therefore, I wanted to ask you to clarify something. Yesterday, when answering certain questions about the El Mujahedin unit and its re-subordination to the 35th Division during the Farz operation, you said that it was not re-subordinated to you during the Farz operation or that you don't recall such an order.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have such an order. I do not recall it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the witness please repeat his answer. It was unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, you are asked to repeat your answer, Mr. Witness. The -- the interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "I did not have that order or I am unable to recall it because -- or rather, as it was before," says the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, I do not wish to lead or suggest an answer to you, but since I am no military expert, if possible could you please explain the following to me: A command conducting a re-subordination of a certain unit to another unit under its command in a certain phase when that unit is no longer needed in that area to which it had been sent by an order on re-subordination, would that command have to return that unit by another order to have it under its own command again?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the right of the commander of the superior command, and he regulates that via an order once a certain operation is concluded during which the re-subordination was supposed to take place. Then that unit is being returned to the unit from which it had come.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, now, in connection with this, this situation concerning the Farz operation, can you recall whether or not you received an order from the 3rd Corps commander returning the El Mujahedin Detachment into his jurisdiction or under his command?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that order, but in the subsequent operations towards the north, the commander took over the competence [Realtime transcript read in error "combatants"] to issue missions and tasks to the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, of course this was many times ago, but could you recall when did he take over the command in subsequent operations that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that the record reflects clearly what was said. At line 9, page 26, the word "combatants" or -- I heard it to say "competence," not "combatants" -- competence. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now I would like to broach another subject. And I'm going to try with your cooperation to illuminate the real relationship between the El Mujahedin Detachment and the forces that you commanded. Now I would like the witness to take a look at Exhibit 434.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, Your Honours, this is a document produced by the 35th Division dated 7th of April, 1995, entitled "Interim order." I apologise, "Preparatory order." My mistake. This document bears the title "Order to prepare," or "preparatory order."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, do you see the B/C/S version of this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The day before yesterday or yesterday - I can't recall exactly - the Prosecutor showed you this document, and you stated that you signed this document; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please focus on item 5 of this document. Take a look at it. Could this order be scrolled down, its English version, so that the Bench may take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We don't -- we don't have the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. This is all right. We are, Your Honours, discussing item 5 of this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, this order was -- states as follows in item 5: As I understand it, you hereby order that the El Mujahedin Detachment be deployed in the area of the Twelfth Kilometre.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But asked by the Prosecutor, you said that you did not establish the base or camp at the Thirteenth Kilometre but that the El Mujahedin did it of their own will. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the Twelfth Kilometre and the Thirteenth Kilometre are not the same geographical location? There is a distance of 1.000 metres between them.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was not the same location in military terms; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the military standpoint, the Twelfth Kilometre facility had more possibilities. It was better equipped.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that the Twelfth Kilometre is a crossroads of major roads?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I'd like to put to you is, being a trained soldier, you had reasons to order this detachment to be quartered at the Twelfth Kilometre; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, therefore, that the El Mujahedin Detachment, without seeking your permission, went and established their camp at the Thirteenth Kilometre; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not obey by my orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with that, you could not do anything else but accept that as a fact on the ground; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I wrote a report to the 3rd Corps command, but I accepted their deployment at that location.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, may we close this document now. And before the break, I would like the witness to take a look at another document, PT2013. For the record, this is an order by the 35th Division dated the 5th of April, 1994. The name by the stamp is Nesad Sabic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was the chief of your staff; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, this is a very brief document. I see that you read it. Have you managed to read it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the usher may scroll down the English version so that the Bench may see it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to clarify something with you concerning this document, please. You see that there is a figure "95" in the number "Strictly confidential 02/2-1-000-376/95." If we could scroll up the English version, please, for the benefit of the Bench. On page 1, of course. Thank you. Can you see, Witness, the date the 5th of April, 1994? Do you agree that this must be a typo in the tape?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is 1995, because the chief of staff arrived in 1995, so this is the 5th -- the 5th of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the 35th Division, it was not established in 1994.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you agree that this is a typo. Now I would like to ask you briefly about the gist of this document. Do you agree that according to what is written here, it seems that Mr. Sabic, chief of staff, is writing a warning addressed to inter alia the command of the El Mujahedin Detachment whereby he points out to very frequent disobedience as for the orders pursuant to which operational and daily reports are to be submitted?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is hereby also ordered that the deadlines for the submission of regular operational reports be honoured. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was regular procedure that units subordinated to you submitted regular and daily combat reports; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Otherwise, you cannot control and command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Now I would like to ask you: Did you receive regular and operational reports from the command of the El Mujahedin Detachment at all?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive any. While they were in my area of responsibility, I received not a single written regular operational -- operational report.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any kinds of reports?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in writing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "not in writing," I'd like to ask you: Did you, as the commander of the 35th Division, receive oral reports from the El Mujahedin Detachment's command?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was analysis after the completion of the Proljece action, and they were present at that analysis briefing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So we -- you are talking about being present during the writing of a written analysis.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. This was an oral analysis at a briefing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly throughout the period when the El Mujahedin Detachment was re-subordinated to you, they attended an oral analysis briefing only once?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The analysis of that combat activity.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which means only once. Now I would like to ask you this: I did not ask you about the -- an oral analysis of a combat activity. I asked you whether you received oral reports about combat activities.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you still going to be long on that point?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wanted to stop here for the benefit of us taking a break, but there were two questions concerning the same matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If we could just deal with a few housekeeping matters before we call the witness. A few things to deal with. First, there is the urgent motion by the Prosecution to -- to -- to lead a witness pursuant to Rule 92 ter. We just want to give you an advance notice given the fact that it's an urgent motion, so that you're not taken by surprise at the last minute. The Chamber, after looking at the response from the Defence, is inclined to deny that motion. A written decision will come down, but we just wanted to give you advance warning so that you can adjust your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If I could just ask for a question of clarification: Is that with respect to all three of the witnesses or the one scheduled for this week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the one scheduled for this week. That's the one to which we have received the response. However, having said that, there is a point that is being raised by the Defence to this motion which seems to -- to be put forward for the future. The Defence is saying that they are -- they are no longer going to voluntarily forego their two weeks' notice on motions, and I don't know how you -- you wish to sort that out between yourselves as parties, but the Chamber cannot at this stage pronounce on motions to which a response has not been filed. So for purposes of what we are saying now, this relates to this motion only. Then there -- there is also the motion by the Prosecution to introduce an item to the 65 ter list of exhibits, to play a video clip but relying on the audio part of it only and not on the video part of it. I just wanted to find out from the Defence, given what you have just said -- what I have just mentioned about the Defence not wanting to forego their two weeks' notice, what is the likely response of the Defence, if any, on that point. Madam Vidovic? Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, if I could respond. The position of the Defence is we would like the full two-week period in order to respond to that matter. And if I can just briefly explain why. We saw from the last motion to which you referred, Your Honour, this -- just a moment ago, in our response we pointed out that in responding hastily, the Defence was, in our submission, caused unfairness. We needed time in order to gain access to jurisprudence which the Prosecution had -- is seeking to rely upon, it was confidential jurisprudence. We weren't able to obtain that. Furthermore, we weren't able to carry out a full review of documentation referred to in that motion. Similarly, in this case, in the motion -- in respect to the motion to introduce the video clip, we would say that this is not a straightforward motion. Now, we are not experts, but from our perusal of the video clip, it's obvious that serious concerns arise. The video clip is an amalgamation of video -- visual images with an audio soundtrack, if I can put it that way. It has therefore been edited. It may be the case that the audio soundtrack is comprised of several different audio recordings which have been put together. The document was placed -- sorry, the video clip was placed on a website known as YouTube. Anybody in the whole world has access to that website and can place these sort of visuals and audio recordings onto the website. We don't have a name for the person who placed it there. What we have is a pseudonym, Hatab72. So, Your Honour, the Defence is seriously concerned about this video clip. We say it's not authentic, and we would like time for two weeks in order to carry out further inquiries. We're carrying out inquiries now, but it's the Defence position that we would need further time in order to -- to continue with those inquiries to formulate our position on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do -- you do understand the Prosecution's position that they don't seek to rely on the video part of the -- of the clip but, rather, on the audio part.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And that's something else, Your Honour, that also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Complicates --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: As far as the Defence is concerned, because as my learned friend stated yesterday, their position as the Prosecution clearly is that they do not seek to tamper or change evidence at all. So we would say that if this document -- if the Trial Chamber does in due course permit the document to be introduced onto the list of exhibits, it should be done as a complete unit and we shouldn't start pulling it apart and breaking it down into components.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. You -- so in other words, the short answer is that you are not able to respond in time for this witness to appear as per schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: That's -- indeed that's correct, Your Honour. And also, just to try and be of some assistance, what we would say is the witness, Aiman Awad, that the Prosecution is proposing to show this video clip to, he is scheduled to testify next Tuesday. It may or may not be the case that perhaps that witness could be rescheduled if the Prosecution really wish to -- to show this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would -- that's why I wanted to establish that, so that I can find out from them whether that witness cannot be rescheduled or whether that -- that clip can't be shown through another witness who's coming later. We just want to find that out from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Are you able to cast a light on those two issues, Mr. Mundis, whether to reschedule or -- or use another witness who's coming later?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Certainly it would be possible to reschedule that witness. Of course, on such short notice, we would not be in a position to bring any -- any other witnesses for those two-day period. That's a separate issue. Of course, a -- another possible solution would be simply for -- I will also state that I do not believe we have any other witnesses who would be in a position to testify about that particular audio clip. Let me, while I'm on my feet, also indicate that another possible course of action would be at this stage to simply allow the Prosecution, if the Chamber were so inclined, to -- to play the tape for the witness, if he were to appear next week, and simply mark it for identification at this point in time, pending later decisions as to whether it could be added to the -- to the exhibit list. I will also, while I'm on my feet, it would be -- it would be helpful, I think, in light of this entire issue, if the Defence could be asked to place their position on the record with respect to this entire, what we've called, farewell ceremony with respect to the El Mujahedin Detachment. That is, it is a bit unclear to the Prosecution the Defence position with respect to that, that gathering. Number one, what's the Defence position with respect to whether there was such a gathering? Number two, what's the Defence position with respect to whether the accused, General Delic, attended that gathering? And what is the Defence position with respect to whether the accused, Rasim Delic, actually spoke at that gathering, assuming he was present and assuming there was such a gathering? Because it goes then to the issue, really, of -- of whether what is purported to be on the audiotape is in fact the accused speaking. So it would seem to us that those issues are all intricately linked together and that would go very much to the issue as to whether we need to reschedule Mr. Aiman Awad's testimony for a subsequent date in these proceedings. In other words, it would be helpful to us to know their position with respect to the three issues that I've -- I've outlined. I do believe they're relevant and go to the very issue as to what steps, if any, we should take with respect to potentially rescheduling this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Before -- before I ask the Defence to -- to respond to what you have just asked, let me just get clarification. First of all, on the question of marking the -- the clip for identification, would the Prosecution then have another witness through whom to tender the -- the clip later, or do I understand you to be saying you play the clip to the witness, you tender it, mark it for identification, the Defence can take their time in their opposition -- in their response to whether or not it should be admitted, and once -- once they have had their two weeks' notice and have responded and you have replied, if there's any need to, we then decide that admission at that time, but without a further witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That would be correct, Your Honour. And again, as we've indicated in the motion, steps have been taken to have the tape forensically examined and -- and the results of that analysis would then be relevant as to whether or not the tape could actually be admitted into evidence at a subsequent date, having given the witness the opportunity to hear it. I state that because, as we've indicated in our letter and -- and filing to the Defence, the witness scheduled to appear next week in his written statement discusses or describes such a farewell gathering and indicates that the accused did in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- attend and address that gathering. And so what -- what we would simply ask would be to lead his oral evidence on that point and then, assuming during the proofing he -- he were to listen to the tape and were -- and were to be able to identify what it is and who it is speaking, we would then be in a position to simply play it for him, mark it, pending responses from the Defence, and from the forensics lab, and obviously in the event that the -- the forensics lab is able to reach any conclusions, we would then put those before Your Honours for a final decision as to whether the tape could then be admitted into evidence. It's simply a -- in effect, a compromised solution so that we can move forward without losing two or two and a half days of our -- of our precious time, in light of the overall schedule whereby we're trying to complete our case prior to the Christmas break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just a couple of points, Your Honour. First of all, obviously the Defence don't want to tell the Prosecution how to schedule their witnesses, but it strikes us that Ismet Alija might be a witness that could be rescheduled at short notice. He's someone who has been in The Hague recently and was proofed and therefore possibly could be someone who could -- could fill the gap. The second point that I'd like to make is that in talking about the video clip as evidence, we seem to be jumping a step. The first step is for the Trial Chamber to decide whether or not to permit the video clip to be added to the Prosecution's list of exhibits. And in the Prosecution motion, they have set that test out as being: Is that in the interest of justice? And what the Defence would say is this: At the moment there is no external objective material from any source which can indicate whether or not the video clip is -- is authentic, and the Prosecution have indicated in the motion that they are getting this video clip verified by a forensic unit. The Defence are also making its own inquiries and we would be proposing some steps in our response. So in our submission, until those external checks, that scrutinization has been carried out, we would say that until that happens the Trial Chamber will not be in a position to decide whether it's in the interest of justice or not to add the video clip to the list of exhibits. If the video clip is added to the list of exhibits, again, when the witness comes -- if Aiman Awad comes to testify next week, the Defence would object strongly to him having -- being shown the video clip during the course of his testimony until we have received the results of those external verifications. So, again, we're going to be in a situation that as soon as the -- the Prosecution attempt to show the video clip to the witness, the -- the Defence will be objecting at that point. So it seems to me -- it seems to us that a few things --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I hear you to be saying is that, in fact, the very motion is premature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Indeed. Absolutely. Absolutely. And as for the farewell ceremony, the Defence will touch upon this in the response, but our view is we're not obliged to deal with this at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Sorry, concerning the farewell -- what my learned friend the Prosecutor stated about the farewell ceremony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: We'll deal with that in our response as far as we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear that. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If -- if I could, Your Honours. Again, I -- I understand the position taken by the Defence with respect to the farewell ceremony, but what -- what we would like to put on the record at this point is simply that, of course, any kind of videotape or audio recording can be authenticated by any number of means, and that does not necessarily rely upon -- exclusively upon any kind of forensic testing. If I have a witness who says he was at such a meeting and heard certain things being said and that tape were then to be played to him and he were to say, that's -- that's exactly what I heard at the meeting, that would be a form of authenticating what's contained on that recording. That's a separate issue from the -- the -- the issue as to whether or not we can add it to the exhibit list. But I do want to make it very clear that our position is that forensic authentication is not the exclusive means by which any kind of recording, whether it's audio or -- or video, can be authenticated, and I don't want to -- to leave the -- the apprehension or the view out there that any and all such material can only be authenticated by -- by means of forensic testing, because I -- I don't believe that's the state of the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yeah. In fact, what I did want to raise with -- with -- what I did want to raise with -- with Mr. Robson but I held myself was: What you indicated earlier, that this witness, if I understood you well, in his statement already does mention that there was such a farewell, that the accused was there, and that he spoke and -- so that he has knowledge of the incident that you are alleging. And -- and you're saying that he would therefore be in a position to authenticate it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That would be the Prosecution position, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. I understand that. And -- and given that, I was surprised then -- it's a little surprising to me that then the Prosecution went ahead and tried to -- to get forensic authentication when, in fact, you had somebody who could authenticate it. But that's what you chose to do. I would like to hear what my colleagues have to say on this. Would you like to say something, Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Apart from losing two, two and a half days, what prejudice would the Prosecution suffer if this witness were to be rescheduled?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That -- that's basically it in a nutshell, Mr. President. We're -- we're doing our best to move along as quickly as possible. If this witness needs to be rescheduled, so be it. There would be no additional prejudice to the Prosecution if we were have -- to have to do that other than trying to meet what we understand to be scheduling commitments, in terms of trying to finish this case, including 98 bis, before the Christmas recess. That's the main concern we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. We understand that. We just have a problem amongst ourselves of the fairness to the accused, which we think overrides that inconvenience.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution understands that, Your Honours. And we will -- if that's the decision of the Chamber, then I will meet with my trial team later this afternoon and determine whether or not we want to proceed with this witness or to attempt to reschedule him. And if we decide to reschedule him, we'll see if there's any other witnesses available. We had already -- over here one of my colleagues passed me a note concerning Mr. Ismet Alija. That would be probably the easiest solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In the event I can't get him, I will endeavour to try to find someone else who's available on short notice to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if that's -- if that violates the Trial Chamber's guidelines, we'll seek leave to add -- to move someone else up if that's the only possible solution, to avoid losing a couple of days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. And if -- if at the end of it all, it means losing those days, then we lose those days. Okay. Okay. Thank you very much. Finally - and I'm sorry to do this, Madam Vidovic - I don't know how many of you do know, but there is this Plenary at 12.00 which we need to go to, and we may not be able to sit for the third session of today. Okay. Thank you very much. May you call the witness. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And perhaps -- perhaps while the witness is being brought in, in light of the Plenary and the -- and the Chamber's oral ruling concerning the 92 ter applications, it -- it appears as though we very well might be in a situation where Friday's witness carries over into Monday and Monday's witness goes into Tuesday. So we very well might end up filling those days anyway without bringing another witness, in light of the current witness and -- and the fact that it -- it appears that he very well might go through the -- through the end of this week. So I just put that on the record, as that might be another obvious solution to this situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave I seek to tender this document, it was PT2013. Could it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 484.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we show PT2059 to the witness. For the record, I wanted to say that this is an order by the command of the 31st Division dated the 8th of the 5th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, have a look at the document. Could we please scroll down so that we can see the signature.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, The 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, did you sign the document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. It is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the document. This order pertains to the forwarding of data on the operative records. Please skim through it. It seems that this document was specifically sent to the El Mujahedin Detachment command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that by this document you requested that there should be a proper, an accurate establishment of operative records in order to assist the overall situation in the unit? Did you request that from the detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at what it says under "order." Can you see the sentence immediately below that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therein you're asking for the records to be established so that you could plan following combat operations. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I wanted to ask you is this: According to the documents we saw, for the first time to you - and when I say "to you," I always mean the 35th Division, not you personally - according to the documents you saw yesterday and today, the 35th Division saw the El Mujahedin being re-subordinated to it for the first time in October 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then there was another order that was dated, I believe, the 31st of March, 1995, re-subordinating the El Mujahedin Detachment to the 35th Division. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Didn't I hear the witness say he didn't receive that order and he doesn't know that order? Before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No. The 35th -- the 31st March 1995. Your Honour, maybe I can be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's the order of June that he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I wanted to ask you, Witness: Once you managed to look through the document, am I correct that irrespective of the fact that that detachment was re-subordinated to you by virtue of an order on the 8th of May, 1995, you did not have any operational records pertaining to the unit whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no data on it, and that is why I drafted this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore on the 8th of May, 1995, irrespective of the fact that that unit had been re-subordinated to you, according to the documents, for six months, you knew nothing about its personnel, manning power, and so on and so forth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to correct something. They were there in October and they left. When they came on the 31st, after the order, then this order was issued subsequently. The re-subordination took place in terms of a given specific task, and then they were returned to their unit, and then returned to me yet again if the commander decided so. Therefore, this was the second re-subordination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Madam Vidovic. Now, this is going to require you to clear with the witness very clearly when they were first subordinated to him, when they left him, when they were re-subordinated. You know, because it doesn't seem to be the same as what we heard before the break now. First of all. Secondly, while I am talking, let me just correct what you said. I think we got confused by the dates. At page 46, line 3, I -- I think you meant to say "31st of March, 1995," and then you said "8th of May, 1995."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said the 31st of March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. But anyway, the transcript says "8th of May, 1995," which is not the order of re-subordination. This is the order calling -- it is this order on the screen. So but here you're saying the detachment was subordinated -- re-subordinated to you by virtue of an order of the 8th of May. So it should be by an order of the 31st of March. That's how it should read?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are correct, Your Honour. Your Honours, I will clarify the matter with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
